links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers with vs without textbook-grounded retrieval on bariatric surgery questions
links.quote: Textbook-augmented RAG produced consistent and significant accuracy gains across all models.

links.outcome: Raw LLM accuracy on domain benchmark showing residual errors in unaided models
links.effect: Raw accuracy was 70.5% (GPT-4o-mini), 81.0% (GPT-4), and 87.0% (GPT-5) on the 200-question benchmark.
links.quote: GPT-4 with RAG reached 89.5% versus 81.0% raw (+ 8.5 pp; +13 questions), and GPT-4o-mini improved from 70.5% to 84.5% with RAG (+ 14.0 pp; +28 questions).

unlisted_practices: Multi-stage RAG pipeline with medicalized query rewriting, query expansion, and LLM-based relevance filtering of retrieved passages
Systematic error analysis of failure modes (evidence-level mismatch, polarity errors, scope misinterpretation, retrieval salience bias)

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounding from an authoritative textbook to baseline LLMs versus raw LLMs on a clinical question-answering benchmark.
